hash_lock.batch_baseline_role: deterministic source baseline and sample-seed INPUT. It is NOT the AC-15 `sample.json` seed.
hash_lock.seed_use: batch_baseline_sha256 pins the exact source bytes this inventory measured, so any source drift invalidates the inventory and everything derived from it. It is NOT the U3 sample seed. computeBatchSample() in tooling/brain/knowledge.mjs derives that seed as sha256 of stable JSON over { batch_id, approved_knowledge_tree_sha256, batch_manifest_sha256, proposal_manifest_sha256 }; the baseline reaches it only transitively, by sitting inside the future batch manifest, and the real seed cannot exist until candidate authoring and proposal generation produce a proposal manifest. Re-verify every source_sha256 and approved_knowledge_tree_sha256_at_inventory immediately before propose and again before apply; a mismatch aborts. `apply` independently refuses with `approved knowledge content changed after proposal generation` if the knowledge tree moved.

selection_rationale.path_coverage: Batch 03 leads with `create` under namespaces the approved index has barely touched: java.operator.* (none applied), java.type.* (1 applied: reference-type), java.variable.* (2 applied: scope, static-variable), java.control-flow.* (1 applied: enhanced-for), plus likely java.literal.* / java.runtime.* / java.encoding.*. It also exercises a SECOND stub-promotion path: software.paradigm.object-oriented-programming is currently a stub and chap01 L42-48 carries an independent assertion about it. REVISION 2 CORRECTION: it is NOT purely a create batch. chap01 L68-95 and chap02 L191/L201-232 assert directly against six already-applied documents (java.oop.class, java.oop.object, java.oop.object-collaboration, java.language.package, java.keyword.final, java.variable.scope), so a meaningful share of the batch is update/no_op rather than create. See existing_touch_points.
selection_rationale.bounded: Four extraction files, 27,033 bytes, 44 heading scopes of which 30 carry prose and 33 are engine-substantive. This is roughly 0.47x batch 02 by bytes and 0.68x by scope count - deliberately the smallest slice since batch 01, because chap01-04 is code-dense rather than prose-dense.
selection_rationale.probes: No file-level probes (discharged by the applied batch 01); 11 in-source zero-evidence scopes provide negative coverage. See rejection_probe_policy.
rejected_alternatives: Re-adopting the three frontmatter-only chapter files as probes: batch 02 conditioned that on a batch-01 REJECTION, which did not happen. Batch 01 applied and already discharged them; re-adopting would double-claim files bound by an applied packet.
Adding kafka chapters to reach a larger batch: different series, no adjacency to the applied Java index, and batch 04+ already owns them split by byte budget.
Splitting chap01-04 into 03a/03b: batch 03 is already the smallest slice since batch 01 (44 scopes vs batch-02's 65), so splitting would add packet overhead without reducing a real review burden.
A consolidation pass over chap05-10 and the pilot chapters instead: worth doing, but it is re-mining applied sources rather than filling the language-basics hole, and it stays scheduled separately.

CONFIDENCE IS LOWER THAN FOR BATCH 02 for two independent reasons: the band was calibrated on prose-dense OOP chapters while chap01-04 is code-dense (30 positive-prose scopes across 27,033 bytes versus batch-02's 53 across 57,373, and only 18 exclusive prose-bearing scopes versus batch-02's 37); and several of the strongest chap01-04 assertions land on ALREADY-APPLIED concepts (see existing_touch_points), so they resolve to update/no_op rather than to new accepted candidates. expected_flagged_for_full_review.code_only_flag_expectation: The 3 code-only scopes should additionally be expected to carry low-confidence or provenance-warning flags if any concept is backed solely by them, because their excerpt is program text rather than an authored assertion.
expected_flagged_for_full_review.sample_quota_recipe: computeBatchSample() sets quota = min(unflagged_pool, max(5, ceil(0.10 x unflagged_pool))) over the UNFLAGGED pool, not 10% of total proposals, and category coverage can add one extra draw per proposal kind missing from the quota slice, so the discretionary count is a floor.
expected_flagged_for_full_review.estimated_u3_review_load: ESTIMATE ONLY, not a mechanical derivation. Under the explicit and unproven assumption that each of the 12 low-evidence scopes yields exactly one flagged proposal and the accepted count lands near the 18 midpoint, the unflagged pool is ~18 - 12 = 6, the quota is max(5, ceil(0.10 x 6)) = 5, and the reviewed set is ~12 mandatory + 5 discretionary ~= 17 proposals plus category-coverage top-ups. Batch 01 is the counterexample that bounds this: 6 low-evidence scopes produced 12 flagged proposals out of 17, so scopes do not map 1:1 to proposals. Batch-02's realised sample was 18 selected of 34.
